traffic.label: LOST TRAFFIC
traffic.body: An image with no description never enters image search. The traffic goes to the store next door whose pictures speak.

agentic.label: LOST AGENTIC SALES
agentic.body: Shopping agents browse your catalog raw. A silent image doesn’t exist to them — and neither does the product.

accessibility.label: ACCESSIBILITY RISK
accessibility.body: The EAA has had ecommerce in scope since June 2025; ADA suits hit thousands of US stores a year. Unreadable images are your most visible gap.

checkbox.title: 100% alt text coverage, still silent.
checkbox.sub: Every bloated SEO suite has an alt-text checkbox. A checkbox stuffs titles into alt fields and calls it done. It doesn’t write like this:
checkbox.beforeTwo: alt="buy mens organic tee best price free shipping SEO"
checkbox.beforeCaption: Junk from filenames and keyword stuffing. Counted as 100% coverage — by the tool that wrote it.
checkbox.afterCode: alt="Moss-green organic cotton tee folded flat, showing the ribbed collar and embroidered leaf at the hem"
checkbox.afterCaption: Every image actually looked at. Distinct per image, ~125 characters, never starts with “image of.”
checkbox.closer: That’s why the free audit <lead>grades instead of counting</lead>: missing / junk / weak / good, with a vision-checked sample. Typical result: “62 of 100 covered images don’t describe the image.” Run it on your store and read the sample yourself — the grade is the proof, not our word for it.

limits.title: What it can’t do.
limits.body: It can’t touch anything except the alt field — structurally. It can’t change your store without your approval. It can’t make an edit that isn’t logged and undoable for 30 days. It can’t overwrite a description a human wrote. And when it can’t reach something (theme-settings images), it flags it with a deep link instead of failing silently.

pricing.trust: Nothing here runs on trust. The audit is free forever, the writing is judged on your own products before you pay a cent, and every change is undoable for 30 days. The only thing we ask you to believe is your own scan.
pricing.footer: Silent images are one of seven leaks. <link>The Leaf suite finds the other six →</link>

breakStore.a: No. It is structurally unable to touch anything but the alt field, every write is verified by reading it back, and every change has a 30-day undo on every plan — with a full before → after trail. It never overwrites words a human wrote, and theme-settings images it can’t reach are flagged with a deep link instead of failing silently.

speed.q: Will it slow my store down?
speed.a: No — it never touches your theme and adds no script to your storefront. It writes alt fields through Shopify’s API and nothing else. Zero front-end weight, zero performance impact.

existingAlt.q: What happens to alt text my team already wrote?
existingAlt.a: Nothing, unless you say so. It never overwrites words a human wrote. The audit grades your existing descriptions — good ones stay, weak ones get flagged with a suggested rewrite, and every decision is yours.

access.q: What does it need access to?
access.a: Products and their images, blog articles and theirs, and your published theme — it reads theme files because that’s where banner and section images live. What it can write is the alt field and nothing else, structurally. No orders, no customers, no payment data.

uninstall.a: The descriptions are yours — alt text lives in your Shopify store, not in our app, so everything you approved stays exactly where it is. App data tied to your store is deleted in line with Shopify’s mandatory data-erasure webhooks, within 48 hours of Shopify’s request.

spam.a: It earned that reputation — we’ve opened catalogs where every description began “image of” and ended in a keyword pile, worse than empty because it looks done. That’s exactly what Image Voice is built against: it looks at every image, writes ~125 distinct characters, never starts with “image of,” and grades the junk that’s already there so you can see the difference on your own store, free.

diy.q: Can’t I just have ChatGPT write my alt tags?
diy.a: For 20 images? Honestly, yes. At 3,000 it breaks: nothing grades what’s already junk, nothing verifies each write, nothing catches the product you upload next Tuesday, and nobody’s watching when it silently stops. Image Voice is the difference between writing alt text once and having it handled — graded, verified, undoable, forever.

rot.q: How do I know the quality won’t rot after I subscribe?
rot.a: Two mechanisms. Writing quality is gated against a fixed golden set — no update can silently degrade what you approved. And a weekly re-scan keeps your number true, catching anything that slips past webhooks. Day-one quality is month-six quality, by construction.

editing.q: Can I edit what it writes?
editing.a: Every description, before it touches your store — approve, edit, or skip from a keyboard queue built for 200 decisions in a sitting. And for 30 days after, everything is still undoable.

matters.q: Does alt text actually matter for sales?
matters.a: Three ways, honestly weighted. Google image search only surfaces images it can read — silent images simply aren’t in the race. AI shopping agents read your catalog as text; an undescribed image doesn’t exist to them. And screen-reader customers hear your products or hear nothing. We won’t tell you it 10×’s traffic — it closes a leak that’s costing you a little, everywhere, forever.

compliance.q: Does this make me EAA / ADA compliant?
compliance.a: No tool can promise that, and we won’t. What it does is close your most visible gap — thousands of unreadable images — with an audit trail to show for it. EAA has had ecommerce in scope since June 2025 in the EU; ADA suits hit thousands of US stores a year.

languages.q: Which languages does it write in?
languages.a: Your store’s own language: English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Dutch, and Portuguese. Your image SEO works in your market — and a German customer’s screen reader speaks German.

seoApp.q: I already have an SEO app with alt text included.
seoApp.a: Run the free audit on what it wrote — that’s the honest test. Most “included” alt text is your product title copied into the alt field: 100% coverage, still silent. The audit grades instead of counting, so you’ll see in minutes whether what you have describes anything. If it’s genuinely good, we’ll be the ones telling you.

firstSweep.q: What’s a First Sweep, and what does the monthly allowance cover?
firstSweep.a: The First Sweep writes your existing backlog up front, in days — you’re not rationed over months. After that, the monthly allowance only has to keep up with new images. On Curator the sweep covers the whole store, theme included.

images.q: Which images are covered — just products?
images.a: Keeper covers your product catalog. Curator covers the whole store — theme images, banners, sliders, section imagery. The audit shows you both numbers, so you’ll know which tier your store actually needs before paying.

hugeCatalog.a: The First Sweep goes after the images that need it — missing and junk descriptions first, not a blind pass over everything you own. And if Curator’s ceiling still isn’t enough for a catalog your size, write to us and we’ll happily work something out. That conversation is cheaper for both of us than a plan that doesn’t fit.
